title: Fixed-Point Correctness Theorem

basis.scope: Introduce bounded fixed-point correctness conditions for admissible continuation expressions. This patch classifies correctness only after admissibility and bounded semantic preservation, without asserting uniqueness or universal existence for all continuation classes.

core_rule.statement: AdmFix(C) is classified as CorrectFix(C) only when EvalPhi(C) preserves the continuation semantics of Fix(C) under every declared bounded application of Phi; bounded fixed-point correctness remains diagnostic, and RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Introduce bounded fixed-point correctness conditions for admissible continuation expressions. This patch distinguishes correctness classification from admissibility while leaving uniqueness, universal existence, and recovery deferred.

canonical_claims.statement: Fixed-point correctness is bounded and applies only after admissibility.
EvalPhi(C) must preserve continuation semantics under declared bounded applications of Phi.
FailCorrectFix(C) classifies correctness failure without asserting uniqueness or universal existence.
Correctness remains subordinate to admissibility and bounded evaluation.

formal_objects.name: Fixed-Point Correctness
formal_objects.definition: The correctness classification assigned to an admissible fixed point that satisfies the declared continuation semantics under bounded repeated applications of the declared fixed-point operator.

formal_objects.name: Fixed-Point Correctness Theorem
formal_objects.definition: An admissible fixed point is correct when bounded evaluation preserves continuation semantics under repeated applications of the declared fixed-point operator.

formal_objects.name: Fixed-Point Correctness Failure
formal_objects.definition: The classified failure state produced when an admissible fixed point fails correctness verification.

correctness_rule.statement: AdmFix(C) is classified as CorrectFix(C) only when EvalPhi(C) preserves the continuation semantics of Fix(C) under every declared bounded application of Phi.

theorem.statement: For every admissible continuation fixed point AdmFix(C), if bounded evaluation preserves the continuation semantics under repeated applications of Phi, then CorrectFix(C) holds.

failure_conditions: Semantic preservation fails under bounded evaluation.
Repeated declared applications of Phi alter the continuation semantics.
The continuation exits the declared admissible evaluation regime.
non_claims: Does not assert universal fixed-point existence.
Does not assert every admissible fixed point is unique.
governance_notes: Correctness is established only after admissibility.
Correctness does not imply existence or uniqueness.
